local.b: Three 6-year-old girls at Henry O. Tanner Elementary in Grand Crossing were taken to Comer Children's Hospital in fair condition with abdominal pain after ingesting an undisclosed substance, officials said.
local.title: 3 kids hospitalized after ingesting 'unknown substance' at South Side school

local.h: Rising rates and prices sideline Chicago buyers
local.b: Hopeful buyers packed North Side open houses over the summer, but agents now report thinner crowds and fewer offers as mortgage rates rise and inventory stays tight, even in hot markets like Lincoln Park.
local.title: Rising mortgage rates and home prices sidelining buyers but now is the time to purchase, report says

local.h: Old Town School teacher Ted Johnson dies at 98
local.b: Johnson taught at the Old Town School of Folk Music from the day it opened in 1957, spending more than 40 years as an instructor and nearly 20 more as a student. Colleagues called him a 'role model' for the school.
local.title: Old Town School of Folk teacher Ted Johnson, who shared ‘magic’ of music with decades of students, has died

local.h: 4 Chicago-area congressional offices get suspicious letters
local.b: Reps. Brad Schneider, Mike Quigley, Robin Kelly and Jan Schakowsky reported letters amid a national wave of threats before Election Day.
local.title: 4 Chicago area congressional offices receive suspicious letters amid wave of preelection threats

local.h: Chicago bids to host 2031 Women's World Cup
local.b: Mayor Johnson sent a letter supporting the bid to U.S. Soccer. The city passed twice on hosting the men's World Cup over taxpayer costs.
local.title: Chicago puts in bid to host 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup

local.h: Big money floods Chicago school board races
local.b: Groups backed by wealthy, often suburban donors have outraised the Chicago Teachers Union 5 to 1 ahead of the Nov. 3 election.

local.h: Suits say delivery robots collect biometric data
local.b: Proposed class actions accuse Coco Robotics and Serve Robotics of scanning customers' faces and hands without consent. Both companies deny it.
local.title: Lawsuits accuse Chicago delivery robot companies of collecting biometric data

local.h: Secret comedy shows pop up in WWII huts
local.b: Don't Tell Comedy is staging secret shows in unexpected spots around Los Angeles, including a surfer-themed bar in a WWII-style Quonset hut at Boardroom Brewery in El Segundo.
local.title: Comedians are holding secret shows in World War II training huts and other random places

local.h: Lawmakers: little progress at Adelanto ICE facility
local.b: Members of Congress who toured the facility Friday described unsanitary showers and kitchens, inedible food and poor medical care.
local.title: Reps say Adelanto has made little progress on unsanitary conditions

goodnews.h: South Pasadena finally has a bookstore
goodnews.b: Outpost Books opened in September in a cozy, just-under-1,000-square-foot space styled like a trading post, with a 'Kids Corral' that plans weekly story readings.
goodnews.title: South Pasadena finally has a bookstore. Step inside Outpost Books

local.h: Man shot near Midtown subway station
local.b: A man was shot Saturday afternoon near the 53rd Street and 7th Avenue station, which serves the B, D and E lines, the NYPD said. Police released no other details, and his condition was unclear.
local.title: Man shot and killed on Midtown subway platform Saturday afternoon, NYPD says

local.h: NYPD seeks Yorkie dognapped in Queens
local.b: Chanel, a 10-year-old Yorkshire Terrier, was taken from her front lawn in College Point late last month when two people in a Subaru Forester scooped her up and sped off, police said.
local.title: Have you seen this Yorkie? NYPD looking for adorable pup dognapped from her Queens home

local.h: Knicks fans adjust to life as champions
local.b: After winning the 2026 NBA Championship, the Knicks will raise their first championship banner at Madison Square Garden in 50 years as they open their season.
local.title: Being reigning champions is weird for Knicks fans, but we could get used to this.

local.h: Tompkins Square Park makeover splits regulars
local.b: A community board committee backed renovating the basketball courts, kids' pool and 1990s outdoor fitness area. Some park users say it goes too far.
local.title: Tompkins Square Park is getting a makeover. Some say it's too much.

local.b: Saturday's protests brought clashes, street blazes and widespread looting, with masked crowds stripping stores. Prosecutors said more than 500 people were held in custody.
local.title: IN PICTURES: France counts cost of violent protests, 1,800 arrested

local.h: Limoges town hall 'largely lost' to protest fire
local.b: Masked protesters set fire to the 143-year-old building, whose roof collapsed onto lower floors, the regional prefect said, calling it 'a catastrophe for heritage.' The fire is now contained.
local.title: Town hall in Limoges 'largely lost' to blaze set during French protests

local.h: A year after heist, Louvre faces uncertain future
local.b: The Louvre is closing security gaps exposed by last year's theft of eight crown jewels, but its reputation has suffered and its aging infrastructure is a growing concern.
local.title: After a year in turmoil, the Paris Louvre faces uncertain future

local.h: Macron tells Le Pen to 'stay humble'
local.b: Without naming her, Macron criticised the far-right frontrunner's plans to cut France's aid to Ukraine and EU contribution. 'Let's show some respect for the men and women of France. They will vote,' he said.

local.h: Macron urges calm before nationwide protests
local.b: Paris banned protests in the city centre ahead of Saturday's cost-of-living rallies, which authorities fear could turn violent.

local.h: Renton may let its Flock camera contract lapse
local.b: The city's license plate cameras have been off since May, and its nearly $170,000 contract expires Nov. 2.
